title: Bonus: Lab Danger Zones + Exam Day

questions.stem: Two lab results return: potassium 6.4 and blood sugar 180. Which does the nurse act on first?
questions.explanation: B is correct: potassium 6.4 is above 5.0 and can trigger a deadly rhythm. A, 180, is high but not an emergency right now. C ignores the priority. D is wrong because potassium 6.4 is abnormal.

questions.stem: For the client with potassium 6.4, which actions are taught?

options.text: Cardiac monitor, notify the provider, expect a repeat level

questions.explanation: B is correct: put the client on a cardiac monitor, notify the provider, and expect a repeat level. A and D add potassium. C delays.
B is correct: glucose 65 is below 70, so give fast sugar. A, C, and D are all in range.

questions.stem: What is the main danger of a potassium level outside 3.5 to 5.0?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the danger for potassium is heart rhythm. A is the danger for sodium. C is the danger for a high international normalized ratio on warfarin. D isn't the potassium danger taught.

questions.stem: A client's sodium is 128. Which complication is the nurse most concerned about?
questions.explanation: B is correct: 128 is below 135, and the danger for sodium is the brain and seizures. A, C, and D aren't the sodium danger taught.

questions.stem: A client on warfarin has a high international normalized ratio. What is the main risk?
questions.explanation: B is correct: too high means bleeding. A is the risk if it's too low. C and D aren't the danger taught for this lab.

questions.stem: Which lab trends signal damage? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct: rising troponin signals heart muscle injury, rising lactate signals poor perfusion, and a potassium climbing from 4 to 5.5 matters because trends beat single numbers. D and E are stable and in range.

questions.stem: Why does the nurse watch lab trends rather than one value?

options.text: A trend tells you more than a single number

questions.explanation: B is correct: a trend tells you more than a single number. A, C, and D are not true or not taught.

questions.stem: Which items belong on the exam-day checklist? Select all that apply.

options.text: An identification that matches it exactly
Bring your study notes into the testing room

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: bring your authorization to test and a matching identification, sleep, eat, and arrive early. E is not on the checklist.

questions.stem: How should a candidate approach a select-all-that-apply item?

options.text: Judge each option on its own, true or false

questions.explanation: B is correct: judge each option on its own, true or false. A, C, and D are not the strategy taught.
